correctness.rationale: The radial spherical transform is derived by one integration by parts from -sech prime and the classical Fourier cosine transform of sech. Its exact sign reduces to lambda*coth(pi lambda/2)-omega*tanh(pi omega/2); the former is strictly increasing from 2/pi, and the latter strictly increases in omega. This yields all necessary/sufficient regimes, the unique negative-frequency band, and the included endpoint. Continuous L2 norm <=4pi/3, and exponentially integrable spectral transform verify the applicable L2-Godement theorem. Independently evaluated direct integrals at 12 points agree to <5e-28 and symbolic transform addition simplifies to zero.

value.rationale: This is the exact admissible oscillation bandwidth of a natural soliton-derived radial kernel after replacing Euclidean distance by geodesic distance on H3. The failure above cutoff is completely localized to one low-frequency spherical band, with an exact transcendental root and no higher-frequency negativity. This structural phase diagram is useful for deciding admissible geodesic covariance models and is not a renaming or unmotivated finite numerical table.
